questions.q: ............ is a contiguous area of memory consisting of equal-size elements
questions.explanation: An **Array** is a contiguous area of memory consisting of equal-size elements, allowing direct index-based access.

questions.q: The Function of adding an element to a stack is called
questions.explanation: **Push(key)** is the standard stack operation for adding (inserting) an element onto the top of the stack.
**Arrays** provide $O(1)$ constant-time access to any element via direct index calculation: `address = base + index × element_size`.

questions.q: The complexity of adding an element to the middle of an array is........
questions.explanation: Inserting into the middle of an array requires shifting all subsequent elements, resulting in $O(n)$ time complexity in the worst case.

questions.q:
The following code is for ........ function

```
node ← new node
node.key ← key
node.next = nil
if tail = nil:
    head ← tail ← node
else:
    tail.next ← node
    tail ← node
```
questions.explanation: This code appends a new node at the **end** of a linked list by updating `tail.next` and advancing `tail` to the new node — which is exactly **PushBack(key)**.

questions.q: Which of the following does not allow homogeneous data elements?
questions.explanation: Arrays don't allow different type elements (An array can only contain one type of elements, e.g., string only, int only... etc).
All fundamental stack operations — **Push**, **Pop**, and **Top/Peek** — run in $O(1)$ constant time because they only operate on the top of the stack.
Stacks follow the **FILO** (First In, Last Out) principle — also known as LIFO (Last In, First Out). The first element pushed is the last one to be popped.

questions.q: PushBack(Key) in a single linked list without a tail is .....
questions.explanation: Without a tail pointer, **PushBack** must traverse the entire list to find the last node before appending, resulting in $O(n)$ time complexity.

questions.q: To return the most recently-added key in a stack, we use the........ function
questions.explanation: **KeyTop(key)** (also known as Peek or Top) returns the most recently added element at the top of the stack **without removing it**.
